root_cause.text: `ice_ptp_setup_pf()` assumed `ice_get_ctrl_ptp(pf)` would always return a valid controlling-PF PTP context, but in VFIO passthrough setups where the PF does not own the source timer, `adapter->ctrl_pf` is never initialized and the NULL return triggers an incorrect `WARN_ON()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (WARN_ON(!ctrl_ptp) || pf->hw.mac_type == ICE_MAC_UNKNOWN)` to an explicit `if (!ctrl_ptp) { dev_info(... "PTP unavailable: no controlling PF\n"); return -EOPNOTSUPP; }`, and the CVE description states that `ice_get_ctrl_ptp()` returns NULL because `adapter->ctrl_pf` is never initialized in that configuration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle missing controlling PF gracefully by returning -EOPNOTSUPP with a log message instead of warning, while preserving the existing MAC-type error path.
intent_record.what: The single conditional `if (WARN_ON(!ctrl_ptp) || pf->hw.mac_type == ICE_MAC_UNKNOWN)` was split into two separate checks: a new `!ctrl_ptp` branch now logs `PTP unavailable: no controlling PF` with `dev_info(...)` and returns `-EOPNOTSUPP`, and the existing `pf->hw.mac_type == ICE_MAC_UNKNOWN` check remains as a separate `return -ENODEV;` path.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now handles the absence of a controlling PF as a normal unsupported-condition instead of triggering a warning, and it provides a clearer error code and log message. The MAC-unknown case continues to fail as before. This makes PTP setup fail more gracefully when no controlling PF exists.
